glosses: Not given to excessive drinking of alcohol.

examples.text: Amid all the confusion and disorder that sin has introduced into the world, the Christian in union with God has a grace or Divine help that enables him to live the sober, self-restrained life.
After eliminating alcohol from their lives, some sober individuals exclusively date nondrinkers.
Rose told me that she's sober.

glosses: Moderate; realistic; serious; not playful; not passionate; cool; self-controlled.

examples.text: God help me to watch and to be sober.
[N]o ſober man vvould put himſelf into a danger for the Applauſe of ſcaping vvithout breaking his Neck.

glosses: Dull; not bright or colorful.

examples.text: Twilight grey / Had in her sober livery all things clad.

glosses: Subdued; solemn; grave.

examples.text: See her sober over a sampler, or gay over a jointed baby.
What parts gay France from sober Spain? A little rising rocky chain.

glosses: Poor; feeble.
To make or become sober.

examples.text: There shallow draughts intoxicate the brain, / And drinking largely sobers us again.
The night air may have sobered him a bit by the time they got back to Beattock.

glosses: To overcome or lose a state of intoxication.

examples.text: It took him hours to sober up.

glosses: To moderate one's feelings; to accept a disappointing reality after losing one's ability to believe in a fantastic goal.

examples.text: Losing his job was a sobering experience.
